verdict.root_cause: The only recorded change to paymentservice in the window is a platform-automation environment update at 09:24:49 that set the OTLP traces export endpoint — previously unset — to a loopback address on port 4317 (tr_eb6ff6f007ba). No collector listens on that in-pod loopback target, so paymentservice's telemetry export path was pointed at nothing: its span-derived call metrics are entirely absent for the window, numerator and denominator alike (tr_54adf3203c6c), and the env mutation would have rolled the pod, which matches the container-hostname change across the unreturned log interval (tr_636b3d98dbb2). Meanwhile the service itself was healthy on both sides of the gap: charge request/complete pairs complete in about a millisecond (tr_636b3d98dbb2), Charge spans are sub-millisecond inside structurally intact frontend→checkout→payment traces (tr_e1a1eb5bf2b3), and checkoutservice's error ratio is a measured flat zero across 61 unbroken samples (tr_3efe7d0db599). The failing mechanism is therefore the configuration value itself — an export endpoint naming the wrong address — which broke the measurement path and produced a no-data page on paymentservice, not a degradation of payment processing.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent request-path signals say the service was serving correctly: application logs show successful sub-millisecond charges before and after the gap (tr_636b3d98dbb2), traces show complete parent chains with no missing payment leg and no error shape (tr_e1a1eb5bf2b3), and the caller's error ratio is a real measured zero rather than absent data (tr_3efe7d0db599). That rules out the classes that require the service to be failing requests: nothing waited on a slow dependency (log timestamps and span durations both foreclose a latency signature), and no image or version rollout is recorded (tr_eb6ff6f007ba explicitly rules out deploy/release events). What is broken is the measurement layer: paymentservice's calls_total series does not exist at all for the window (tr_54adf3203c6c), and the single recorded change repointed telemetry export to a loopback target six minutes before the page (tr_eb6ff6f007ba). The wrongness of that address is the failure — it is why the metric is missing and why the alert fired — which is bad_config rather than a downstream consequence of some other mechanism. Reverting the endpoint variable to the real collector address is the fix; the pod restart already implied by the hostname change did not restore the metric series, so restart alone is insufficient.
open_questions: The metrics specialist left open whether the absent calls_total series means no emission or a different metric/label naming; nothing dispatched distinguished these, so 'telemetry broke' is inferred, not measured.

The trace listing carries no per-span timestamps and was truncated at 200 spans (tr_e1a1eb5bf2b3), so it is unknown whether any spans postdate 09:24:49. If trace export continued after the repoint, the loopback endpoint was not fully dead and the missing-metrics explanation weakens.
The log result omitted roughly 09:21:17–09:31:09 — the interval containing the 09:30:45 alert time. Whatever the service actually did at the moment it paged is uncovered by any dispatch.
No dispatch retrieved the alert definition or firing condition, so it is not established that the page was a no-data/absent-series alert rather than something else.
The change query covered only 09:20:45 onward (tr_eb6ff6f007ba); anything that landed in the preceding hours is unexamined.
Triage reported two unmeasured edges crossed and a third affected service that was never dispatched; whether the same telemetry repoint or an unrelated fault touched them is unknown.

Whether the exporter pointed at a dead loopback target caused queue backpressure or startup blocking inside the pod (an exhaustion mechanism) was not measured — no process- or container-level resource metrics were collected.
